title: Prove exact incomparable-demand fanout tariffs over Z/n
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

PR #5045 leaves incomparable demand ideals open, starting with `(2,3)` over `Z/6`. This proves the exact optimum for that instance, gives all five attaining words and proves that their count vectors are the complete Pareto frontier. For arbitrary positive stationary coefficient-independent prices, with `c_i` charging ADD into row i:

```text
OPT = min(mu0+mu1, 2mu0+2c1, 2mu1+2c0,
          mu0+2c0+2c1, mu1+2c0+2c1).
```

The additional algebra also extends #5045's piecewise five-term formula to **every demand pair over every Z/n, n >= 2**, including incomparable ideals with a nonunit common generator. Given demands x,y, the new construction chooses `beta=x-a*y` with `(beta)=(x,y)`, using an elementary CRT argument. Writing `y=r*beta` then gives a single-insertion, four-ADD word with exact dirt restoration. The arbitrary-word source-count lower bound and directional return lemma are credited to #5045 and restated in the self-contained proof.

Only `research/z6-incomparable-fanout/` is added (five files). This is a scoped written algebraic proof with exact finite corroboration, **no new κ**. Exactly two arbitrary dirty rows, one preserved disjoint source, and full dirt restoration are required. Extra rows, observers, coefficient-dependent physical prices, arbitrary noncommutative incomparable ideals, a physical caller and compiler/outer admission remain outside scope. No independent human or proof-kernel acceptance is claimed.

## Task and overlap

- Scientific base: freshly fetched canonical main `81e9bd69e4a5b00ba9c713a1620e36d576d5522e`; unchanged at the submission refresh. Priority revision 7; selected κ remains `60403/20000000`.
- Explicit donor assignment takes #5045 Open next question 1. `bit-helper-contract` is marked **changed**, preserving the full original card and explaining the algebraic side-result boundary.
- [Canonical investigation comment in #5030](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/5030#discussioncomment-19141722).
- #5045, Krzysztof Wójt, retained head `8639d7b6348d9b09683e71d74afcceedf2d4bdc0`: proof and README are pinned by Git blob and SHA256 at the new base, as provenance. No predecessor executable is imported or rerun.
- Initial and submission overlap checks include targeted all-state `incomparable`/`fanout`/`5045` searches and the live #5030 thread. The submission snapshot covers 307 open PRs (08:39 UTC) and 4,212 Discussion records (08:41 UTC), with complete reported remote pagination. No resolving successor or conflicting active claim was found in that coverage. Local note coverage is sparse; arbitrary diffs, omitted notes, unpublished work and later activity are not exhaustively covered.

## Validation

At contribution head `ba325c0b94bc69d2a0d264bec581899f220d4613`, standard-library Python 3.12 on macOS:

- 119 complete affine-state Dijkstra runs, comparing **3,654 exact optima**. All demand pairs over Z/2 through Z/6 are covered; the 5,184-state Z/6 graph is searched at 91 price vectors. The oracle uses only primitive transitions and does not call the formula or word constructors.
- 9,830 ordered CRT checks, 24,575 attaining-candidate words, 147,450 forward/inverse basis checks and 2,160 literal Z/6 scalar-state checks. The word checks cover every demand pair over Z/2 through Z/24 plus larger composite fixtures.
- Sixteen built-in controls cover invalid domains, the false unit-demand shortcut, missing dirt restoration, wrong coefficients and necessity of every envelope term. Three additional disposable semantic mutations reject: missing restore gate, omitted mixing charge, and wrong oracle prices.
- Registered normal and optimized replay, exact source pins, committed-byte preflight and official export integrity pass. Normal and optimized direct replay also pass from a read-only Git-free export with `PATH=/nonexistent`; all six exported files remain unchanged.

```sh
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/z6-incomparable-fanout --check-only
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/z6-incomparable-fanout
python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/z6-incomparable-fanout
```

The universal conclusion rests on the written CRT and arbitrary-word proofs, not extrapolation from the finite price/modulus checks. No selected-construction cold replay, Lean or Docker was needed for this isolated result. Optional full source-history ancestry checking was not run in the shallow checkout. Hosted CI passed both planning and the registered package replay at this exact head in [run 39926839937](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/39926839937). This is replay evidence, not mathematical acceptance.

## Credit

Prepared by lee-phys with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance in derivation, implementation, checking and writing; Apache-2.0. Credit Krzysztof Wójt #5045 for the source-count lower bound, directional return lemma and comparable-demand result; Nick Petalas #4916 for the ring-valued contract; Ross Richardson #3121/#3063; Cinna Davis #1944/#1968; Anthony #774; Oscar Fennell #759; Tekalign #3130; and the retained lineage. No novelty is claimed for CRT or the inherited lower-bound argument.

## Open next questions

README and TASK give first steps and blockers for the one-insertion orbit over other rings, three-row nonunit demand `(2,1,1)` over Z/4, and one actual caller with a complete physical tariff matrix. The residue-ring two-row question is resolved within the stated contract; these extensions remain separate.
